paper_title: Exotic energy injection in the early universe II: CMB spectral distortions and constraints on light dark matter
notes: Black 'CMB anisotropy (our work)' contour of Fig. 10, extracted from the vector paths of the e-print file figs/ALP_constraint.pdf (solid black stroke, width 2.5) with axes calibrated on the tick-label positions (log-log, ~78 pt/decade in mass, ~42.3 pt/decade in g). This is the paper's own recast of its extended Planck CMB anisotropy power-spectrum lifetime constraint on DM -> gamma gamma (Fig. 9, based on rescaling the Planck 2015 TT/TE/EE limits of Slatyer & Wu, their Ref. [9]) into g_agamma via Gamma = g^2 m^3 / 64 pi. Cross-checks: the low-mass end (~31 eV, near m = 2R_Rydberg = 27.2 eV) corresponds to tau ~ 4e25 s, consistent with the quoted tau >~ 1e25 s at m = 2R; at 1e6 eV the curve corresponds to tau ~ 2e24 s, consistent with Fig. 9. Cosmological decay bound assuming ALPs are all of the dark matter; no local-DM-density rescaling applies. Confidence level not stated explicitly in this paper; the underlying Planck anisotropy constraints are 95% CL. The last point lies at the clipping edge slightly beyond the 1e6 eV axis limit of the figure.
